one_line: Restorer of Pandya rule in Madurai after the Kalabhra interregnum.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, athletic and wiry, with the calm poise of a seasoned but still vigorous king.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, medium-brown Dravidian complexion, high cheekbones, sharp black eyebrows, and a thin, neatly kept moustache; eyes are large, dark, and steady, with a default expression of composed determination and quiet resolve.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair drawn back into a high, tight topknot (kudumi) at the back of the crown, sides smoothed; front hairline clean; wears a simple, narrow gold circlet resting above the forehead with a tiny central fish emblem.
appearance.costume: He wears a knee-length off-white cotton angavastra-style wrapped lower garment (veshti) with a broad deep-blue border edged in gold, pleated neatly in front and tied at the waist; over his torso he has a fitted, short-sleeved, pale-cream cloth tunic reaching mid-thigh, belted with a plain brown leather belt; a deep-blue upper cloth with a subtle gold fish motif along the edge is draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back like a royal shawl; his feet are in simple brown leather sandals; jewellery is modest but regal—medium-width gold armlets on both upper arms, a single gold bangle on each wrist, small round gold earrings, and a thin gold necklace with a small fish pendant; there are no fantasy elements, just finely woven early-medieval South Indian textiles with light, realistic folds.
appearance.signature: A long, slightly curved iron sword with a plain steel blade, a simple unadorned cross-guard, and a dark brown wooden hilt wrapped in leather, worn in a brown scabbard hanging from his left hip belt; he often holds a small triangular hand-banner with the Pandya twin-fish symbol in deep-blue on an off-white cloth.

ref_desc: Kadungon is a mid-30s, medium-brown king with an oval face, thin moustache, black hair in a high topknot with a narrow gold circlet, wearing an off-white veshti with deep-blue and gold borders, cream tunic, deep-blue fish-motif shawl, modest gold jewellery, and brown sandals, carrying a plain curved iron sword at his left hip and a small deep-blue twin-fish banner, with off-white, deep blue, gold, brown leather and black as his dominant colours.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Kadungon, restorer of Pandya rule in 6th-century Madurai: a mid-30s, athletic South Indian king with a medium-brown complexion, oval face, straight nose, thin neat moustache, large steady dark eyes, and thick black hair pulled into a high topknot at the back of the crown, topped with a narrow gold circlet bearing a tiny central fish emblem; dress him in a modest, historically plausible early-medieval South Indian outfit: a knee-length off-white cotton veshti wrapped and pleated in front with a broad deep-blue border edged in gold, a pale-cream short-sleeved tunic that reaches mid-thigh under a simple brown leather belt, and a deep-blue upper cloth draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his back, its edge subtly patterned with a repeating gold fish motif; add modest royal jewellery—medium-width gold armlets on his upper arms, a thin gold necklace with a small fish pendant, small round gold earrings, and a single gold bangle per wrist—plus simple brown leather sandals; at his left hip hangs a plain, slightly curved iron sword in a brown scabbard, with a simple cross-guard and dark wooden hilt wrapped in leather, and in his hand he holds a small triangular hand-banner, off-white cloth with the Pandya twin-fish symbol in deep-blue; use a palette dominated by off-white, deep blue, gold, brown leather, and black, and present front, side, and back views to clearly show his consistent face, hair, costume, jewellery, sword, and banner details.
